speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To narrow down the cause of these symptoms, which began first and have you been experiencing any numbness or muscle wasting?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest, alongside diplopia on upward/downward gaze, strongly suggests a neuromuscular junction disorder. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis) or difficulty chewing/swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: The absence of recent infections and symmetrical weakness helps narrow the differential. Have you noticed a significant variation in the strength of your limbs during a single day, or do you experience fatigue in your eye muscles when reading?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had trouble swallowing or slurred speech. I also have not noticed breathing difficulty, and the symptoms started gradually about a month ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The absence of bulbar symptoms like dysphagia or slurred speech, combined with a one-month history of fluctuating weakness and gaze-dependent diplopia, points toward a specific neuromuscular junction issue. Do you experience a distinct worsening of your double vision or weakness towards the end of the day or after prolonged use?

text:
The electrical studies showing normal nerve conduction and no significant jitter effectively rule out Myasthenia Gravis and neuropathies. Given the combination of gaze-dependent diplopia, proximal muscle weakness (difficulty climbing stairs), and upper limb weakness without sensory loss or autonomic involvement, I need to know if you have a history of thyroid disease or recent heat exposure before finalizing the plan.
